page_title: Threadlines ADE: desktop app for Claude Code, Codex and more

sources.entry: Threadlines - Open-source desktop app for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor), where several agents can share one thread and each thread gets its own git worktree. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Threadlines/threadlines) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Threadlines
summary.one_liner: Threadlines is a free, open-source desktop app (an "agentic development environment") for running Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other coding agents together in one thread.
keywords: run several agents in one thread
use_cases: Run Claude Code and Codex side by side on the same task
Review GitHub pull requests alongside the agent conversation
Give each agent task its own isolated git worktree
Schedule recurring coding agent tasks or trigger them from GitHub issue labels
Let one computer's agent start threads on another linked computer
summary.what_it_does: Threadlines lets you add more than one coding agent (such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Cursor) to a single thread and switch between them without losing the conversation. Each thread can get its own Git worktree so agents work in separate checkouts. Pull requests, CI status, file diffs and Git history can be viewed beside the chat, and a built-in browser lets you attach page screenshots to messages. Agents can start new threads, and scheduled tasks can run prompts at set times or when a GitHub issue gets a label, while the app is running. The page also describes linking several computers into one "fleet" so an agent on one can start a thread on another.
notable: Open source under MIT license, source on GitHub, began as a fork of T3 Code
Multiple agents in one thread with per-thread git worktrees
Fleet feature links several computers so agents can start threads on each other
Built-in browser with screenshot attach and GitHub PR review with CI status
caveats: Scheduled tasks run only while Threadlines is running on that computer
Agents are used with the user's own existing agent accounts; the page does not describe any paid tiers
Agent-initiated threads and fleet features ask for permission by default
